patches.value: For all I=[a,b] with 0<=a<=b and h=b-a<=1, all 0<=sigma<=1 and paths f_j in L^infty(I;H^sigma) with weak derivatives in L^infty(I;H^(-pstar)), Ctri satisfies ||C_I(f1,f2,f3)||_2<=C*h*product_j||f_j||_(X(I))+C*||f_i||_(L^infty H^(-pstar))*product_{j!=i}||f_j||_(L^infty L^2), each i=1,2,3. For time-independent inputs, ||C_I(f1,f2,f3)||_2<=C_sigma*h^sigma*product_j||f_j||_(H^sigma), including sigma=0. For 0<sigma<=1 choose a_sigma=1/2-sigma for sigma<1/2, a_sigma=1/8 for sigma=1/2, a_sigma=0 for sigma>1/2. Then 0<=a_sigma<1, and for every f in H^sigma and g in H^a_sigma, ||fg||_2<=C_sigma||f||_(H^sigma)||g||_(H^a_sigma). For any constant mean-zero w in H^sigma with ||w||_(H^sigma)<=M, 0<tau<=1 and a>=0, sup_[a,a+tau]||F_a(t;w)||_(H^a_sigma)<=C_(M,sigma)*tau^sigma and sup_[a,a+tau]||F_a(t;w)||_(H^(1+sigma))<=C_(M,sigma). All these are in the normalized norms, with constants uniform in endpoints and support.

There is an absolute C>0 such that the following bounds hold uniformly in time. For mean-zero f,g in L^2 and all real t, ||Dinv f||_(H^1)+||Dinv f||_infinity<=C||f||_2, ||B_t(f,g)||_(H^(-pstar))<=C||f||_2||g||_2, ||J_t(f,g)||_(H^1)<=C||f||_2||g||_2, and ||Dinv P(fg)||_2<=C||f||_2||g||_2. For mean-zero A, ||A||_(H^(-pstar))<=||Dinv A||_2 whenever the latter is finite; ||J_t(A,g)||_2<=C||Dinv A||_2||g||_2. For all A,A2 in H^1, the algebra bound is: ||A*A2||_(H^1)<=C||A||_(H^1)||A2||_(H^1). S_t is unitary in every H^s, preserves reality/mean and is strongly continuous. For continuous, piecewise time-smooth spatially smooth mean-zero paths f,g on [a,b], integral_a^b B_t(f,g)dt=(1/3)[J_t(f,g)]_a^b-(1/3)integral_a^b[J_t(f',g)+J_t(f,g')]dt. Also J_t is symmetric and integral_I J_t(B_t(f,g),h)dt=C_I(f,g,h). In particular F_a(t;f,g)=[J_s(f,g)]_(s=a)^(s=t)/6 for constant inputs. All bounded product maps extend from polynomials by density.

For a smooth real mean-zero exact KdV solution u on [0,T], twist v=S_(-t)u, and smooth Scheme trajectory f_n=S_(-t_n)U^n, suppose M>=1+sup_[0,T]||v||_(H^gamma), 0<tau<=1, delta_n=||f_n-v(t_n)||_2<=1 and q_n=tau^gamma+delta_n. Then Interp satisfies sup_(I_n)||rho_n||_2<=C_M*tau*q_n and ||mathcalR'||_(L^infty(I_n;H^(-pstar)))<=C_M*q_n. On any I=[a,b] contained in [0,T] with a a grid point, h=b-a<=1, define e=v-V and E_I=sup_I||e||_2. If E_I<=1 then sup_I||mathcalR(t)-mathcalR(a)||_2<=C_M*(h+tau)*(tau^gamma+E_I), ||e||_(X(I))<=C_M*(tau^gamma+E_I), and ||v||_(X(I))+||V||_(X(I))<=C_M. Intervals may end inside a step; derivative assertions hold a.e. All constants depend only on M,gamma,T and are uniform in n,tau and Fourier support.
Apply at source base t_0=0, stage time s in [0,tau], inputs f=g=S_a w and beta=a_sigma. The displayed Airy-conjugation identity transfers the H^a_sigma bound to F_a(a+s;w,w).

value.bindings: Apply separately at source base t_0=0, stage time s in [0,tau], inputs f=g=S_a w and beta=1+sigma. The source time exponent is zero; the Airy-conjugation identity transfers this H^(1+sigma) estimate to base a.
hypothesis_checks: L1 and the displayed unitary Fourier calculation give 0<sigma<=1, tau>0 and constant mean-zero H^sigma inputs S_a w on [0,tau].
The upper endpoint beta=1+sigma is in [beta0,1+sigma], as verified in F002.

patches.value: Use sigma=gamma, b=T, q_source(x)=-q(-x) and B0=R for the positive-regularity flow and a priori bound.

value.bindings: In the smooth-data clause, take arbitrary higher Sobolev order sigma>gamma, horizon b=T and reflected source datum -q(-x), with B0=R. Uniqueness identifies these higher-order flows with the gamma-order flow.
hypothesis_checks: In this conditional clause q is smooth, real and mean-zero, reflection preserves these properties, and H001 gives T>0.
Smooth q has a finite homogeneous norm at every chosen sigma>gamma>0, so the positive-regularity existence and uniqueness clauses apply.
Its initial L^2 norm is <=R by L1; clause(iv) is not used here.
